Sergio, it is Marina. I have read the memo from the committee and I want you to have my view before Wednesday. First, the good news. Nobody in that room is against this deal. Every objection you got is a condition, not a no. Second, and this matters, do not answer all three with the same energy. The fee is not the real one, even though it is the easiest one to argue about, and if you spend twenty minutes on it you will look like a man defending a number instead of a man solving a problem. Third, the concentration. That is the real one, and I think we can answer it. Ask Nordbank for a cap written into the contract, and speak to Meridian about taking forty of the one hundred and eighty. Although Meridian moved slowly last time, they will take a piece of a deal that is already priced. One more thing, and it is about tone. When you answer an objection, agree with the part that is valid before you turn. If you tell the committee their concern is wrong, you have lost them, however good the rest of your answer is. Call me tonight.

Sergio, Paulo here, from the credit desk. Two minutes on how to answer an objection, and then I will leave you alone. The shape is always the same and it has two halves. In the first half you give the other side their point. Not a small version of it, the real one, in their own words. You are right that one percent is more than we paid last year. In the second half you turn, and the turning word is although, or even though, or however. Although the fee is higher, the five year cost of this package is lower than anything else on the table. Both halves matter. If you only do the second half, you sound like a man who has not listened. If you only do the first half, you have agreed and the meeting is over. And here is the part that people get wrong, and it is small. The turn is not a but. In English, when you open with although, you do not put a but in the second half. Although the fee is high, we accept it. Never although the fee is high, but we accept it. It is a tiny thing and it is the thing that makes you sound like someone who has done this before. See you Wednesday.

First, write the objection down in the other side's own words. Then say clearly which part of it is valid. Next, turn with although, even though or however, and give your strongest fact. After that, offer the condition that answers the concern, not the whole deal. Finally, agree the next step and the date.
